docs.title: Git Workflow
docs.text: This page describes the Git workflow adopted for MUSICO software development, with a focus on the use of bare repositories.

docs.title: Bare Repository
docs.text:
A bare repository is a Git repository that contains only the version-control data (the contents of a normal .git/ directory) with no working tree. It is created with:

git init --bare <repo-name>.git

Because it holds no checked-out files, a bare repository is designed exclusively to receive and serve commits — it is never edited directly.

docs.title: Why MUSICO Uses Bare Repositories
docs.text: Concern Bare repository behaviour Central server storage No working-tree files means no accidental edits on the server and a smaller footprint. Multi-developer push/pull Bare repositories accept git push from any number of clients without the "refusing to update checked-out branch" error that a normal repository produces. CI/CD integration Deployment hooks (post-receive, post-update) fire reliably after every push, letting the server automatically build or deploy the MUSICO software without manual intervention. Backup and mirroring A bare clone (git clone --mirror) reproduces every ref exactly, making it the correct form for backup targets and read-only mirrors.

docs.title: Typical Directory Layout
docs.text:
/srv/git/
└── musico.git/          ← bare repository (central server)
    ├── HEAD
    ├── config
    ├── description
    ├── hooks/
    │   └── post-receive  ← deployment automation
    ├── info/
    ├── objects/
    └── refs/

Developer workstations clone from the bare repository and push changes back to it:

Developer A  ──push/pull──┐
Developer B  ──push/pull──┼──► /srv/git/musico.git  (bare)
Developer C  ──push/pull──┘

docs.title: Setting Up a Bare Repository
docs.text:
On the server:

# initialise a new bare repository
git init --bare /srv/git/musico.git

# or mirror an existing repository
git clone --mirror <existing-remote-url> /srv/git/musico.git

On a developer machine:

# clone from the bare repository
git clone <user>@<server>:/srv/git/musico.git musico

# add it as a remote in an existing local repo
git remote add origin <user>@<server>:/srv/git/musico.git

docs.title: post-receive Hook Example
docs.text:
Place an executable script at /srv/git/musico.git/hooks/post-receive to trigger automated actions after every push:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy to the staging environment after every push to main
while read oldrev newrev refname; do
    if [ "$refname" = "refs/heads/main" ]; then
        echo "Deploying MUSICO to staging..."
        GIT_WORK_TREE=/opt/musico/staging git checkout -f main
    fi
done

Make it executable:

chmod +x /srv/git/musico.git/hooks/post-receive
